mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE is below 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 < 1% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month averages signals a robust demand environment, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both RSAFS and HOUST exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the federal funds rate followed by a sustained decline over the next three months signals a policy pivot from tightening to easing, which lowers discount rates and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps then declines for three months after
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive after a FEDFUNDS spike followed by three months of decline.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) is inconsistent with normal labor market dynamics and signals potential data anomalies or sectoral shifts, which increase uncertainty and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both increase in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 1% for three consecutive months signals a risk of deflation, which increases real debt burdens and discourages consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL < 1% for three consecutive months.
